name: Daybound Delivery Date for WooCommerce
author: Edinson Moreno

sections.description:
Daybound Delivery Date for WooCommerce lets your customers choose a delivery date in the WooCommerce block checkout. It is built on the official Block Checkout Integration API and the Store API, so the date field appears inside the checkout form, uses WooCommerce’s own validation, and is saved with the order.

When a shopper picks a date, the calendar disables anything they shouldn’t choose — past days, days inside your lead time, blackout dates, and anything beyond your maximum window — and the choice is re-validated on the server before it is ever trusted. Leaving the date empty blocks “Place Order” using WooCommerce’s own native validation, not a custom error box. The selected date is saved to the order as HPOS-compatible order meta and shown to you in the orders list and on the order detail screen.

Features

  • Delivery-date picker injected into the block checkout via the official Integration API (not legacy checkout hooks).
  • Calendar that disables past dates, sub-lead-time dates, and dates beyond your maximum future window — all computed in your store timezone.
  • Configurable minimum lead time, maximum future window and blackout dates (holidays, closed days) from a settings page.
  • Native “Place Order” blocking when no date is selected (WooCommerce validation store).
  • Server-authoritative revalidation of every date via the Store API — client checks are never trusted.
  • Delivery date saved to the order as HPOS-safe meta (_daybound_delivery_date).
  • “Delivery Date” column on the orders list (HPOS and legacy) and a read-only date on the order detail screen.
  • The chosen date is shown back to the customer in the order totals (order confirmation and order details).
  • Calendar months and weekdays follow your site language and “week starts on” setting.
  • A page reload keeps the date the shopper already picked.
  • Graceful fallback to a native date input if the calendar ever fails to render.
  • Fully translatable (ships a .pot plus Spanish translations) and accessible (labelled calendar, live-region announcements).
sections.installation:
1. Make sure WooCommerce 8.3 or higher is installed and active, on PHP 8.0+ and WordPress 6.6+.
  2. Upload the daybound-delivery-date folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  3. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  4. Go to WooCommerce → Delivery Settings and set your minimum lead time and maximum future window.
  5. Open your block checkout — the Select a delivery date field appears inside the checkout form.

The plugin declares High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) compatibility, so it works whether or not you have HPOS enabled.
sections.faq:
Does this work with the block checkout?

Yes. The field is added through WooCommerce’s official Block Checkout Integration API, so it renders inside the checkout form and uses native validation.

Does it work with the classic (shortcode) checkout?

No. Version 1.0 targets the modern block checkout, which has been the WooCommerce default since 8.3. If your store still uses the classic shortcode checkout, switch to the block checkout to use this plugin.

Is it HPOS compatible?

Yes. The plugin declares custom_order_tables compatibility and reads/writes order data exclusively through the order object API ($order->get_meta() / $order->update_meta_data()), so it is correct on both HPOS and legacy storage.

Can a customer bypass the date rules by calling the API directly?

No. Every date is re-validated on the server by an authoritative validator that derives all boundaries (today, lead time, blackout list, timezone, maximum window) from your server configuration and ignores anything the client claims. The calendar’s disabling is a UX convenience, never the security boundary.

What happens if something goes wrong during checkout?

The plugin is designed to never break a purchase. If the calendar fails to render, it falls back to a native date input. If the date can’t be saved at order time, the order still completes without a date and the issue is logged, so you can contact the customer to agree on one. Internal failures are written to WooCommerce → Status → Logs (source daybound-delivery), never shown to the shopper.

Is it translatable?

Yes. All user-facing strings (PHP and JavaScript) use the daybound-delivery-date text domain, and the plugin ships languages/daybound-delivery-date.pot. JavaScript strings are wired with wp_set_script_translations().
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
  • Delivery-date picker injected into the block checkout via the official Integration API.
  • Store-timezone calendar that disables past, sub-lead-time, beyond-maximum, and blackout dates.
  • Native VALIDATION_STORE_KEY blocking of “Place Order” when no date is selected.
  • Server-authoritative Store API revalidation; client checks are never trusted.
  • HPOS-safe order meta persistence (_daybound_delivery_date) and admin orders-list column + order-detail display.
  • Settings page for minimum lead time and maximum future window (capability-gated, nonce-protected).
  • Resilience: Error Boundary with native date-input fallback; safe config defaults; missing date never blocks the order.
  • 500 ms client debounce, 10 s request timeout (AbortController), and per-session 2 s server rate limit.
  • Full i18n (ships .pot, registers JS translations) and accessibility (labelled calendar, live regions, aria-describedby).
  • Fixed the textdomain-too-early (_load_textdomain_just_in_time) notice by deferring dependency-notice translation to after init.
